technical_and_efficacy.assessment: The only efficacy evidence is an issuer-reported mouse proof-of-concept study (B1). Sample size, design, protocol, endpoints and publication are absent, and the issuer's p-value reading is overstated (B2). The issuer itself says it does not know whether the results will translate to humans (B3). Nothing documents a technical failure, so R-TECH-1 is unknown rather than adverse. This is animal data only. It is not demand, regulatory or human evidence. The patents are issuer-listed, and nothing shows they cover SELtx (B19).

commercial_demand.assessment: The company has no revenue (B6). The $408M-$734M revenue figures are an issuer projection built on assumed pricing and penetration, with no payer, clinic or distributor commitment (B7). The product is not available for human use. Under R-DEM-1, missing demand evidence for a pre-commercial company is unknown / stage-appropriate, not adverse.

regulatory_progress.assessment: Milestone by milestone: (a) IRB review: only a planned step, with no submission or approval documented. (b) FDA interaction or authorization: none documented. (c) Trial initiation: none. (d) Human efficacy: none. The 2026 timing is conditional on funding and on equipment not yet delivered (B5). No regulatory action against the company is documented; the previous-offering rescission risk is an issuer hypothetical. Status is unknown / not adverse (B4).

team_execution.assessment: The documented team is a founder with a 1973 PhD in neurosciences, a business development VP, an interim CFO who is a consultant, and a CTO who was an IT consultant (B17). The table shows no prior clinical-trial, device-regulatory or commercialization record. The issuer states there are no bad-actor disqualifications. No sanction is documented, so R-TEAM-1 is not adverse. Documented relevant track record is thin.

financing_and_runway.assessment: Audited cash was $19,213 at 2025-12-31, against FY2025 operating cash outflow of $50,743 and liabilities of $268,348 (B8). Unaudited issuer-stated cash is $160,487.20 at 2026-06-18 with a claimed ~6 months of runway (B9). K5 withheld a runway calculation because no spending figure is current, so the six-month figure is an issuer claim only. The Form C says substantial doubt exists, while the audit report and Note 4 do not (B11). The cost of the human trial and devices is not stated. The target raise allocates only $30,000 to clinical trials (B10). The adverse test for R-FIN-1 (cannot reach the next milestone even with the maximum raise) cannot be assessed: no cost of the next milestone is given, and the maximum raise allocates $2.18M to trials. Result: unknown.

terms_and_investor_proceeds.assessment: Common stock at an arbitrary $1.00, with no cap or conversion feature. K1 gives illustrative arithmetic of $75,000,001 on 75,000,001 shares held by the founder. K2 and K3 are withheld, and K4 is withheld because the note conversion terms are undisclosed (B12). Investors give a 10-year irrevocable proxy to the founder (G8), hold through a custodian, and have no anti-dilution or return preference (G4-G6) (B13). Dilution and priority sources are two existing notes ($60,000 and $150,000, described as senior debt, with an unexplained extra $50,000 and an undisclosed conversion price), a planned $50,000 MOU note, $199,875 owed to the founder, 2% intermediary securities, and a reserved right to issue senior stock (B14). The fees are issuer-paid and no investor-paid fee is stated; the issuer pays them from proceeds, as is ordinary (B15). The Charter and note instruments are not in the pack (B18). No priority allocation to insiders, no repurchase below price, and no uncapped nominal-price insider issuance is documented. Consideration for the 75,000,000 founder shares is not stated.

competition_and_advantage.assessment: The 'only later-stage non-pharma solution' and 'no peer or competitor' statements are unverified issuer assertions. They conflict with the preclinical-only data. The pack also cites 107 active ALS trials, 50+ drugs in development and three approved drugs, including generic riluzole at $276-$360 a year (B16). No third-party competitive analysis is in the pack. No substantiated advantage is shown beyond the unreplicated mouse data.
